key_insight: CME-AQA combines first-person and third-person video with visual-pose fusion to improve automatic action-quality assessment for complex TCM rehabilitation skills like acupuncture and Tuina.
clinical_relevance: It could support more convenient, scalable training evaluation for structured hands-on procedures where self-occlusion and hand-object interaction make single-view assessment unreliable.
method: Cross-view multimodal framework using both first-person and third-person videos
Visual-pose fusion to capture context plus body/hand motion
Trained and tested on dual-view TCM-AQA61-A and TCM-AQA61-T datasets
evidence_signal: On the collected dual-view datasets, the method outperformed or matched competitive baselines, with over 10% relative F1 improvement on key rating tasks and lower error on quantitative measures; it also showed comparable results on a CPR dataset.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on structured, recorded assessment settings, so real-world deployment may still depend on camera setup consistency, annotation quality, and generalization to broader clinical environments.
paper_title: Cross-view Multimodal Vision-Based Assessment Framework for Traditional Chinese Medicine Rehabilitation Training
